artifacts.summary: 7-phase deletion plan for FormalSystem/FrameConditions/ (853 .lean lines, 6 paths), sequencing a green build baseline first, the typst prose rewrite before deletion, the C11 Boneyard waiver inside the deletion batch, and a final four-gate sweep.

memory_candidates.content: When deleting a source directory in a repo whose documentation gates are TEXT-GREP based (e.g. typst-sync-check.sh check 1, which only requires a backticked identifier to occur somewhere in some .lean file), the gate can be passing for the wrong reason: retirement/deprecation PROSE inside the doomed files is itself what satisfies the grep. Deleting the files therefore converts currently-passing identifiers into new violations, so a naive 'delete then fix docs' order undercounts the damage. The correct sequencing is to rewrite the prose-side references FIRST, drive the text-grep gate to zero at pre-deletion HEAD, and only then delete -- which both pre-empts the trap and clears any inherited debt in the same paragraph. Corollary for reachability-based invariant checks: a gate that counts UNREACHABLE modules is unaffected by deleting a REACHABLE one, and adding a manifest entry for a just-deleted module actively fails such a gate. Verify which population an invariant counts before assuming a deletion moves it.
